In this article, we explain how to get to Help and support and review your different support options from within the admin center.

updates.after:
### Run diagnostics on the Tunnel server

Use `mst-cli diagnose` on an installed Tunnel server to check known prerequisites and configuration requirements, including those required for logging. Run diagnostics when expected logs are missing or a log upload fails.

To run diagnostics and review the logging checks:

1. Connect to the Linux server that hosts the affected Tunnel Gateway.
2. Run the following command on the server:

   ```bash
   mst-cli diagnose
   ```
3. Review the logging results. Each logging check reports a pass or fail status and the expected result. The output also includes fixes for some common failures. Checks and corrective steps vary with the server's operating system and installation.
4. For a failed check, compare the result with the expected result and follow the corrective guidance provided for your configuration. Run `mst-cli diagnose` again after making changes.
5. [View the Tunnel logs](#view-microsoft-tunnel-logs) to check whether the expected entries are present. If you're investigating an upload failure, follow [Troubleshoot missing logs or failed uploads](#troubleshoot-missing-logs-or-failed-uploads) to verify collection and upload separately.

The command creates a report named `diagnosticReport.txt` in `/etc/mstunnel/diagnostic`. You can share this report with Microsoft support for further analysis.

Diagnostics identify known unmet prerequisites. They don't identify or interpret every operating system customization or hardening setting that might affect Tunnel. A pass result applies to the check performed; it doesn't confirm that every customization is compatible or that logs were uploaded successfully.

### Troubleshoot missing logs or failed uploads
If expected Tunnel logs are missing or **Send logs** reports a failed upload, use the following steps:
1. [Run diagnostics on the affected Tunnel server](#run-diagnostics-on-the-tunnel-server). Review the logging checks and address failures using the guidance in the output.

2. Check the [logging prerequisites](prerequisites.md#validate-logging-prerequisites), including access to the required upload endpoints. If the server uses a customized or hardened operating system, review whether those changes affect the requirements identified by diagnostics.
3. [View the local Tunnel logs](#view-microsoft-tunnel-logs). Local log entries and passing diagnostic checks don't confirm that logs reached Microsoft.

4. After addressing the identified failures, repeat the [Send logs procedure](#easy-upload-of-diagnostic-logs-for-tunnel-servers). Reproduce the issue during the eight-hour verbose collection period, and check the status of each log set in the admin center. An **in progress** status isn't a completed upload. The second log set is collected and uploaded after the eight-hour period.
5. If collection or upload still fails, contact Microsoft support. Include the diagnostic report, the failed checks, and the collection times and statuses shown in the admin center.

# Audit Windows devices against CIS benchmarks with Microsoft Intune

Use the Center for Internet Security (CIS) audit baseline in Microsoft Intune to assess Windows 11 devices against the CIS Microsoft Intune for Windows 11 Benchmark. Create an audit profile, assign it to device groups, and review the results to identify configuration gaps.

CIS auditing is in public preview. It's audit-only: assigning the profile doesn't configure settings or remediate findings.

Before you begin, review the tenant, license, device, and permission requirements in Prerequisites.

## Prerequisites

Before you create an audit profile, confirm the following requirements:

- **Tenant and license:** An Intune tenant with [Microsoft Intune Advanced Analytics](../../advanced-analytics/index.md).
- **Devices:** Windows 11 devices [enrolled in Intune](../../device-enrollment/enroll-devices.md). For co-managed devices, set the **Device configuration** workload to **Pilot Intune** or **Intune**.
- **Permissions:** To create and manage audit profiles, use an Intune role with the following permissions:

  - **Organization** > **Read**.
  - **Security baselines** > **Assign**, **Create**, **Delete**, **Read**, and **Update**.
  - **Device configurations** > **View Reports** to view audit reports.

  The [Endpoint Security Manager](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/ref-built-in-roles.md#endpoint-security-manager) built-in role includes the profile-management permissions. You can also add permissions to a [custom role](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/create-custom-role.md). Your role also needs access to the relevant [scope tags](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/scope-tags.md) and target device groups.

#### Manage Windows Server devices with Microsoft Intune (Insider preview)
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Windows Server management in Microsoft Intune is for testing and evaluation in nonproduction environments only. Microsoft doesn't support production use of Windows Server management in Intune.

Microsoft Intune now includes management for eligible [Windows Server Insider preview builds](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/windowsinsiderpreviewserver). Use familiar Intune workflows to manage Windows Server devices alongside Windows devices.
> [!NOTE]

> Only [Windows Server Insider preview builds](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-insider/business/server-get-started) can be enrolled in Microsoft Intune. Server enrollment is not supported in production Intune environments.

> Windows Server management in Intune and the Windows Insider Program are available through opt-in. Follow the linked registration and download instructions, then register and sign in before downloading a build.

> This is prerelease software. Windows Server Insider Preview builds may be substantially modified before they are commercially released. These builds are for testing purposes only, and not for production use. Microsoft is not obligated to provide any support services for this preview software.

This preview includes persistent physical servers and virtual machines (VMs) running Desktop Experience, including persistent single-session hosts. Server Core, multisession, ephemeral, and nonpersistent hosts aren't included.
Before enabling server enrollment, review existing Windows policy and app assignments. Use dedicated server pilot groups and assignment filters to separate servers from Windows devices.

Server enrollment is blocked by default. To opt in, allow server devices in your enrollment restrictions profile. For details, see [Blocking server devices](../device-enrollment/restrictions.md#blocking-server-devices).
On enrolled pilot servers, you can:
- Apply supported device configuration and endpoint security policies, including settings catalog policies, custom configuration profiles, and administrative templates.
- Evaluate supported compliance policies and use device compliance with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access.
- Deploy and monitor Win32 apps.
- Configure supported Windows Update ring settings.
- View device inventory and policy, app, and compliance status.
- Use supported remote device actions, such as sync, restart, BitLocker key rotation, and diagnostic collection.
Azure and Azure Arc aren't required to manage Windows Server devices in Intune. Azure Arc provides complementary Azure governance, monitoring, automation, and hybrid or multicloud services.
To learn more about Windows Server management in Intune, see [Get started with Windows Server management in Intune](https://aka.ms/IntuneServerGuide).

**Help shape what's next:** Tell us what works, what's missing, and which server-management scenarios matter most to you. Submit the [Intune Server Management preview feedback form](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/ax1xF5ccUC) or visit the [Windows Server Insiders community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/category/windows-server/discussions/windowsserverinsiders). For preview issues, use these feedback channels instead of contacting Microsoft support.
Applies to:
- Windows Server

This audit-only capability doesn't configure settings or remediate findings and requires Microsoft Intune Advanced Analytics.

### CMG update to version 2609 fails when Azure permissions or resource provider registration are missing
Starting in version 2609, Configuration Manager automatically disables shared-key access for cloud management gateway (CMG) storage. Existing CMGs that previously used shared-key access also require Azure role-assignment permissions and resource provider registration for this transition. A successful deployment on an earlier version doesn't confirm that these prerequisites are met.
If the CMG server application's service principal can't create the required storage role assignments, the CMG deployment update can fail. **CloudMgr.log** can report HTTP `403`, `DeploymentFailed`, and a denied `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` action. Missing **Microsoft.Maintenance** resource provider registration can also cause the deployment update to fail.
Before updating, verify the CMG server application's effective permissions at each CMG resource group. The **Contributor** role alone doesn't grant storage role-assignment permissions, and the signed-in administrator's permissions don't establish that the CMG application has access. Use the constrained role-assignment configuration described in [Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app](../../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad.md#configure-azure-rbac-permissions-for-the-server-app), rather than granting unrestricted administrator permissions.
Also verify that **Microsoft.Maintenance** is registered in every Azure subscription that hosts a CMG. Registration in a staging subscription doesn't register the provider in a different production subscription. For instructions, see [Configure Azure resource providers](../../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad.md#configure-azure-resource-providers).
updates.after:
## OS deployment

### Task sequence status messages fail in the full OS with CNG/KSP boot media certificates

*Applies to: version 2609*

After you upgrade to Configuration Manager version 2609, task sequences that use boot media with an imported public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate backed by a Cryptography Next Generation (CNG) key storage provider (KSP) might fail to send status messages after restarting from Windows PE into the full Windows OS.

**smsts.log** records error `0x80072f9a` (`ERROR_WINHTTP_CLIENT_CERT_NO_ACCESS_PRIVATE_KEY`). Each failed attempt to send a status message is retried, adding delays to OS deployment. The Windows PE phase isn't affected.

To work around this issue, import the certificate's private key into a legacy cryptographic service provider (CSP), export the certificate and private key to a new Personal Information Exchange (PFX) file, and recreate the bootable media.

Use an RSA certificate with an exportable private key. Protect the PFX files and their passwords from unauthorized access.

1. Open a Command Prompt window in the folder that contains the original PFX file. Run the following command to import the certificate into the current user's **Personal** certificate store by using the **Microsoft Enhanced RSA and AES Cryptographic Provider**:

   ```console
   certutil -user -csp "Microsoft Enhanced RSA and AES Cryptographic Provider" -p "<pfxpassword>" -importPFX My boot-media-original.pfx
   ```

   Replace `<pfxpassword>` with the original PFX file's password and `boot-media-original.pfx` with its file name.

updates.summary: This article was newly captured in the tracker. This does not establish when Microsoft first published it or released a feature.
updates.after:
# Require Google Workspace authentication on Android with Microsoft Intune

Use a Microsoft Intune device configuration policy to require users to authenticate with a managed Google Account from your organization's Google Workspace domain. This policy gives users access to the Google apps and services assigned to their organizational account.

This feature supports corporate-owned fully managed devices, corporate-owned devices with a work profile, and personally owned devices with a work profile. Use the settings catalog for supported corporate-owned devices and a device configuration template for personally owned devices with a work profile. Corporate-owned dedicated devices aren't supported because they aren't associated with an individual user.

After a user authenticates, the managed Google Account replaces the device's managed Google Play account. The policy doesn't change the Microsoft Entra account associated with the managed device.

Before you create the policy, prepare a managed Google domain enterprise and managed Google Accounts. Review the [prerequisites](#prerequisites) for domain verification and administrator roles.

## Prerequisites

- A managed Google domain enterprise connected to Intune. Upgrade an existing Managed Google Play enterprise if required. For connection and upgrade steps and required Intune permissions, see [Connect Intune to managed Google Play](../../device-enrollment/android/connect-managed-google-play.md#upgrade-to-a-managed-google-domain). The administrator performing the upgrade also needs the **Super Admin** role in Google Workspace during the upgrade.
- A verified Google Workspace domain. For instructions, see [Verify your domain for Google Workspace](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/domains/verify-your-domain-for-goog

updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Update to BitLocker Recovery Key Process for Windows Autopilot”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before: Microsoft Intune is changing how BitLocker resets occur for reused Windows Autopilot devices in the September (2309) service release. Previously, users could access the BitLocker recovery key via BitLocker self-service when reusing devices that were configured through Windows Autopilot. However, after the change, users will need to contact their IT admin to request a restore or to access the BitLocker recovery key. IT admins will continue to have full access to recovery keys both before and after this change.
updates.after:
Microsoft Intune is changing how BitLocker resets occur for reused Windows Autopilot devices in the September (2309) service release. Previously, users could access the BitLocker recovery key via BitLocker self-service when reusing devices that were configured through Windows Autopilot. However, after the change, users will need to contact their IT admin to request a restore or to access the BitLocker recovery key.

IT admins who aren't owners of these devices continue to have access to recovery keys both before and after this change. IT admins who own an affected device are subject to the same BitLocker self-service restriction, even if they have administrative permissions. These admins need to contact an IT admin who isn't an owner of that device to retrieve its recovery key.

The Managed Home Screen (MHS) is an Intune app that allows you to configure the home screen on the device. It only shows the apps that your users access and the device settings that admins need to manage.
The MHS is used for kiosk devices, including frontline worker (FLW) devices. It replaces the default launcher on your Android Enterprise dedicated and fully managed devices. To learn more about the MHS app, go to [Configure the Microsoft MHS app for Android Enterprise](../../app-management/configuration/configure-managed-home-screen.md).

This approach helps you configure Managed Home Screen (MHS) and supports Intune app scenarios that need permission before the app can bring an experience to the foreground.
Before you begin, review the prerequisites later in this article. ## Week of May 11, 2026

### Device enrollment

#### Complete Platform SSO registration during macOS Automated Device Enrollment

On macOS devices enrolled with Automated Device Enrollment (ADE), you can run Platform SSO during device registration. Before you enroll, you:

1. Create an Intune [settings catalog policy](../device-configuration/settings-catalog/index.md) and configure the **Enable Registration During Setup** setting.
2. Deploy the Company Portal (5.2604.0 and newer) as a line-of-business app.
3. Configure the Automated Device Enrollment policy to use Setup Assistant with modern authentication and enable await final configuration.

When this feature is enabled, users have access to Microsoft Entra ID resources immediately when they arrive at desktop.

To learn more, see [Configure Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) during Automated Device Enrollment for macOS devices](../device-configuration/settings-catalog/configure-platform-sso-during-enrollment.md).

Applies to:

- macOS 26 and newer
- Company Portal 5.2604.0 and newer

## Week of May 4, 2026

### Monitor and troubleshoot

#### Enhanced app inventory with faster data updates

Intune enhanced app inventory brings faster, more detailed visibility into the apps in your environment to support identification of outdated or risky software. Improved data freshness and richer app metadata provide clearer insight into installed applications, while new controls let you specify which devices are included in inventory collection.

This feature is initially available for Windows, with additional platforms to follow.

Applies to:

- Windows 10/11

### Maintenance windows for updates on Windows devices

Microsoft Intune will introduce maintenance windows to help you schedule firmware, driver, and operating system updates on Windows devices. You'll be able to choose supported update operations and configure a start date, start time, duration, and repeat schedule.

You'll create a maintenance windows profile in the Microsoft Intune admin center to define when update activity should take place. # Configure local actions for Android devices in Microsoft Intune

Android local actions let you configure actions that run directly on managed Android devices when supported device events occur. By pairing triggers with actions, you can make devices respond to events such as a device reboot, a Managed Home Screen sign-in, or a change in the device's power connection.

You can use local actions to launch apps, send broadcasts to apps, initiate a global sign-out, or exit Managed Home Screen from kiosk mode.

## Prerequisites

- An Android device enrolled as a [dedicated device](../../device-enrollment/android/setup-dedicated.md) or [fully managed device](../../device-enrollment/android/setup-fully-managed.md).
- For activity actions, Overlay Permission (`SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`) granted before you deploy the policy. For more information, see [Overlay permission for foreground app launches](#overlay-permission-for-foreground-app-launches).

## Create the profile

To configure local actions, create a device configuration profile using the **Local actions** template.

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
2. Select **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **Configuration** > **Create** > **New policy**.
3. Select the following properties:

   - **Platform**: Select **Android Enterprise**.
   - **Profile type**: Select **Templates**.
   - **Template name**: Select **Local actions**.
4. Select **Create**.
5. In **Basics**, enter the following properties:

   - **Name**: Enter a descriptive name for the policy.
   - **Description**: Enter a description for the policy. This setting is optional but recommended.
   - **Profile type**: Select **Corporate owned devices**.

updates.after:
# Configure maintenance windows for Windows updates in Microsoft Intune

Use maintenance windows in Microsoft Intune to control when automatic Windows Update actions can begin on managed devices. You can restrict downloads, installations, and update-related restarts to a scheduled period.

Maintenance windows help you plan updates for devices that need to remain available during operating hours, such as kiosks, shared devices, and manufacturing equipment. Configure a one-time window or a recurring daily, weekly, or monthly schedule.

Maintenance windows govern Windows Update content, including quality updates, feature updates, Hotpatch updates, .NET updates, drivers, and firmware. They don't determine which updates are approved or offered to a device.

## Before you begin

Before you create a policy:

- Confirm that devices are enrolled in Intune and run a supported Windows version. The underlying maintenance window settings require Windows 11, version 24H2 with KB5077181, build 26100.7840, or later.
- Confirm that you have Intune permissions to create, configure, and assign device configuration policies.
- Identify a device group for your initial deployment. Test the policy on representative devices before assigning it more broadly.
- Review the update policies assigned to those devices, including deferrals, deadlines, grace periods, and expedited updates.

For the underlying Windows settings and operating system requirements, see [Update Policy CSP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-update).

## How maintenance windows work

A maintenance window controls when the automatic update actions you select can begin. Actions that aren't selected continue to follow other applicable Windows Update policies.

updates.summary: The captured article wording changed. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
The list of requirements for Windows Autopilot device association is organized into four categories:

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> Device association requires a **physical device**. Virtual machines aren't supported.
Device association requires a **physical device**—virtual machines aren't supported. Each device must have **TPM 2.0**, enabled and in a good state. The TPM shouldn't be in **Reduced Functionality Mode**. TPM attestation is enforced during association: device association uses the TPM to attest the device's identity before enrollment.
updates.after: The list of requirements for Windows Autopilot device association is organized into five categories: - **Hardware** - Physical device and Trusted Platform Module (TPM) requirements. - [![](../../images/icons/configuration-18.svg) **Hardware**](#tabpanel_1_hardware) ### Hardware requirements > [!IMPORTANT] > > Device association requires a **physical device**. Virtual machines aren't supported. TPM attestation is enforced during association: device association uses the TPM to attest the device's identity before enrollment. TPM requirements: - Each device must have TPM 2.0, enabled and in a good state. - The TPM shouldn't be in Reduced Functionality Mode. - TPM must be [FIPS 186-3](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/fips) or newer compliant. - TPM must support [TLS 1.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9846#section-4.3.3).

## Client management
### Clients aren't able download content from CMG when branch cache is enabled
*Applies to: version 2403*
After Branch Cache is enabled on primary sites, clients are unable to download apps and packages from the cloud management gateway (CMG). They typically manage to download only 20-30% of the content before the process gets stuck. In some cases, after downloading certain blocks of packages from the CMG, clients look for Branch Cache to retrieve the remaining content. However, none of the clients are able to download the complete content from the CMG, which prevents others from using Branch Cache to access it. The **CTM.log** on the client includes entries similar to the following:
```log
(CTM.log - CTMJob({63B4C4CE-2DC4-4062-93C7-E5019B3B6CE1}): CCTMJob::Start - State=DownloadingContentFromPeers)
CTM.log _- CTMJob({D21758B0-D895-474E-9695-1023A25A1770}): CCTMJob::_PerformDownloadWithOutBranchCache - Download failure using branchcache, fallback to regular download
To work around this issue, disable branch cache.
> [!NOTE]
>
> Clients are able to download content from the on-premises distribution point when Branch Cache is enabled.

*Applies to: version 2309 with KB25858444 and later*

## Set up and upgrade
### ODBC driver version 18.7.1.1 can block site configuration before updating to 2609
*Applies to: upgrades to version 2609*
Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server version [18.7.1.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/windows/release-notes-odbc-sql-server-windows#187) has a known issue with Configuration Manager version 2603 and earlier that can block site configuration.
To avoid this issue, don't install ODBC driver version 18.7.1.1 before updating Configuration Manager. Use ODBC driver version [18.6.2.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/windows/release-notes-odbc-sql-server-windows#186), the validated version shipped with Configuration Manager 2609, for the update. Complete the Configuration Manager update to version 2609 before you install ODBC driver version 18.7.1.1.

updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “ESP tracking”. Compare the added wording and its surrounding context below.
updates.after:
### PowerShell script execution during ESP

PowerShell scripts can run while the Enrollment Status Page (ESP) is displayed. However, ESP doesn't track PowerShell scripts as blocking workloads or wait for them to complete successfully. ESP can complete when its tracked applications and policies meet the configured ESP criteria, even if a PowerShell script is still running.

At startup, the Intune management extension processes PowerShell scripts first, then starts Win32 app processing in the same startup flow. This ordering doesn't guarantee that all PowerShell scripts finish before any Win32 app processing begins. Other device check-ins or notifications can independently trigger app processing while a script is still running.

Don't rely on ESP or the Intune management extension startup order to ensure that a PowerShell script completes before a Win32 app starts installing. If an app requires a script or another prerequisite to complete before installation, include that prerequisite as part of the Win32 app deployment.

# Become a Microsoft Intune Mobile Device Management Partner

The Third-Party Compliance MDM Partner Program is designed for mobile device management (MDM) solutions that determine and manage compliance for user-associated devices and use Microsoft Entra ID to communicate device compliance status to Microsoft services.

## Supported scenarios

To be eligible as an Intune compliance partner, your MDM solution must meet the following criteria:

- Manage devices using MDM protocols.
- Evaluate device compliance for user-based scenarios.
- Use Microsoft Entra ID for user identification.
- Support one or more of the following platforms: Android, iOS/iPadOS, and macOS.

Partners interested in integrating with Microsoft should begin by creating a Microsoft Entra app for their MDM product. For instructions, see [Register a Microsoft Entra app and create a service principal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-create-service-principal-portal).

After you create a Microsoft Entra app and obtain a Microsoft Entra app ID, you can apply to become a partner through the [Intune Compliance MDM Partner Application](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/GKYuFnrSdv).

Microsoft uses the submitted information to validate that:

- The solution aligns with the intended Intune and Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access scenario.
- The proposed integration is appropriate for the Intune Device Compliance API.
- The partner is prepared to provide enterprise-grade support to customers after launch.

updates.title: Manual registration overview
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Platforms for device registration; Manually register devices with Windows Autopilot”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
Ideally, the OEM, reseller, or distributor from which the device was purchased performs the registration of a device with Windows Autopilot. However it's also possible to register devices manually. A device might need to be registered manually if:
- The device was obtained from a non-participant device manufacturer or reseller.
The following diagram shows how manual registration and OEM registration might be used to deploy both new and existing devices with Windows Autopilot.
![Screenshot that shows Windows Autopilot device registration process.](images/image2.png)
To [manually register a device](add-devices.md), a device's hardware hash first has to be captured. Once this process is completed, the resulting hardware hash can be uploaded to the Windows Autopilot service. Because this process requires booting the device into Windows to obtain the hardware hash, manual registration is intended primarily for testing and evaluation scenarios.
> Customers can only register devices with a hardware hash. Other methods (PKID, tuple) are available through OEMs or CSP partners as described in the previous sections.
- [Microsoft Intune](add-devices.md) - Intune is the preferred mechanism for all customers.
- Partner Center - Partner Center is used by CSP partners to register devices on behalf of customers.

updates.title: Overview of Windows Autopilot device preparation
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Windows Autopilot device preparation improvements; Improved experiences”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
- **Support for Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Department of Defense (DoD) environments**. Windows Autopilot device preparation supports [GCCH and DoD](../../intune/fundamentals/government-service.md) environments.
Windows Autopilot device preparation supports device association, which binds a physical Windows 11 device to your tenant before enrollment. Associated devices are automatically marked as corporate-owned and can receive device-targeted policy assignments and additional OOBE customizations. For more information, see [Overview of Windows Autopilot device association](device-association/overview.md).
updates.after:
### Cloud environments

Windows Autopilot device preparation supports [Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Department of Defense (DoD)](../../intune/fundamentals/government-service.md) environments.

The device association capability isn't yet available in sovereign cloud environments.
Device association uses a device's Trusted Platform Module (TPM)-backed identity to establish a trusted relationship with your tenant before enrollment. The association is stored in the device's Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) firmware and verified during onboarding.

Use device association to:

- Assign a device preparation policy directly to a device, regardless of which user signs in. A device-based policy assignment takes precedence over a user-based assignment.
- Automatically mark the device as corporate-owned.
- Apply a device name template during enrollment.
- Customize OOBE settings, such as language and keyboard configuration, and hide selected setup pages.

Device association is optional. For the full capabilities and lifecycle, see [Overview of Windows Autopilot device association](device-association/overview.md).

updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “How are purchased apps licensed?”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before: - Installing apps up to the number of licenses you own.
updates.after:
- Installing apps up to the number of licenses you own, or without a fixed license quantity for apps with unlimited licenses.

### Unlimited assets

Intune supports assigning VPP apps with unlimited licenses from Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager on iOS/iPadOS and macOS devices. For these apps, you don't need to acquire additional license quantities as your deployment grows.

Apple refers to apps and books that an organization owns as *assets*. Free apps and books support unlimited assignment by default. However, organizations can choose to retain their existing fixed inventory for an organizational unit. Don't assume that every free app has unlimited licenses for every location. Paid apps still require sufficient purchased licenses for your assignments.

To deploy an app with unlimited licenses:

1. In Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager, acquire the free app for the location associated with your Intune location token.
2. In the Intune admin center, select **Tenant administration** > **Connectors and tokens** > **Apple VPP tokens**, select the token, and choose **Sync**. For more information, see [Synchronize a VPP token](#synchronize-a-vpp-token).
3. Assign the synchronized app to your groups as described in [Assign a volume-purchased app](#assign-a-volume-purchased-app).

Unlimited licenses remove the need to manage a fixed license quantity. They don't change the device and user licensing requirements or assignment restrictions described in this article.

> [!NOTE]
>

updates.title: What is co-management?
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Benefits; Prerequisites”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
Co-management is one of the primary ways to attach your existing Configuration Manager deployment to the Microsoft 365 cloud. It helps you unlock more cloud-powered capabilities like Conditional Access.
You're also able to pilot a workload with a separate collection of devices. Piloting allows you to test the Intune functionality with a subset of devices before switching a larger group.
[![Overview diagram of co-management.](media/co-management-overview.svg)](media/co-management-overview.svg#lightbox)
> When you concurrently manage devices with both Configuration Manager and Microsoft Intune, this configuration is called *co-management*. When you manage devices with Configuration Manager and enroll to a third-party MDM service, this configuration is called *coexistence*. Having two management authorities for a single device can be challenging if not properly orchestrated between the two. With co-management, Configuration Manager and Intune balance the [workloads](#workloads) to make sure there are no conflicts. This interaction doesn't exist with third-party services, so there are limitations with the management capabilities of coexistence. For more information, see [Third-party MDM coexistence with Configuration Manager](coexistence.md).
When you enroll existing Configuration Manager clients in co-management, you gain the following immediate value:

## Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app

The CMG uses the **server/web application's service principal** to deploy and manage its Azure resources. These Azure role-based access control (RBAC) permissions are separate from the Microsoft Entra directory roles used to create app registrations. Assign permissions to the server application's service principal, not the native/client application or the user who runs the console.

Starting in version 2609, shared-key access is automatically disabled for CMG storage. Existing CMGs that previously used shared-key access also need the permissions for Microsoft Entra-authenticated storage and storage role assignments. A successful deployment or update on an earlier version doesn't confirm that these permissions are present.

Verify the following effective permissions at each CMG resource group:

- **Resource management:** Retain the **Contributor** role or equivalent approved permissions that allow the server application to manage the CMG resources.
- **Storage role assignments:** Allow the server application to manage assignments of the **Storage Blob Data Contributor** and **Storage Table Data Contributor** roles. Contributor alone doesn't grant `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write`.

To provide the storage role-assignment permissions with limited delegation:

1. In the Azure portal, open the CMG's resource group and select **Access control (IAM)**.
2. Identify the service principal for the CMG server application. Verify its application (client) ID and service-principal object ID against the application used by Configuration Manager.
3. Review its existing role assignments, including inherited assignments and their conditions. If equivalent effective permissions already exist, don't add a duplicate grant.

articles.title: About discovery methods for Configuration Manager

before.text: - To discover a computer resource by using Active Directory system discovery, the discovery agent must be able to resolve the FQDN of the resource. If it can't resolve the FQDN, it then tries to resolve the resource by its NetBIOS name.

- To discover a user or group resource by using Active Directory user discovery or Active Directory group discovery, the discovery agent must be able to resolve the FQDN of the domain controller name that you specify for the Active Directory location.

For each location that you specify, you can configure individual search options, like enabling a recursive search of the location's Active Directory child containers. You can also configure a unique account to use when it searches that location. This account provides flexibility in configuring a discovery method at one site to search multiple Active Directory locations across multiple forests. You don't have to configure a single account that has permissions to all locations.

When each of these three discovery methods runs at a specific site, the Configuration Manager site server at that site contacts the nearest domain controller in the specified Active Directory forest to locate Active Directory resources. The domain and forest can be in any supported Active Directory mode. The account that you assign to each location instance must have **Read** access permission to the specified Active Directory locations.

# Bulk registration token verification fails after installing Configuration Manager 2603 update rollup

*Applies to: Configuration Manager (current branch, version 2603 with update rollup KB39169655 installed)*

## Summary of KB40345593

This update resolves a token verification issue that occurs after you install the [update rollup for Microsoft Configuration Manager version 2603 (KB39169655)](39169655.md).

After you install the update rollup, bulk registration token verification fails on the management point for devices that aren't Microsoft Entra joined and connect through a cloud management gateway (CMG) to obtain a Configuration Manager-issued client authentication token.

This issue affects the [bulk registration token](../../core/clients/deploy/deploy-clients-cmg-token.md#bulk-registration-token) scenario and may also affect other scenarios in which devices that aren't Microsoft Entra joined communicate through the CMG. It doesn't affect devices that use Microsoft Entra authentication.

On the management point, errors similar to the following are recorded in `<MP_InstallDir>\Logs\CCM_STS.log`:

```text
ProcessRequest - Start
Incoming request URL: https://<management-point>/CCM_STS
Validated PreAuth SelfProve token. UniqueId: <client-id>. ClientKey: <public-key>
ProcessRequest - Exception: System.IO.FileLoadException:
Could not load file or assembly
'mpisapiclr, Version=5.0.9146.1045, Culture=neutral,
PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35' or one of its dependencies.
The located assembly's manifest definition does not match the assembly reference.
(Exception from HRESULT: 0x80131040)
```

As a result, affected devices can't complete bulk registration through the CMG to obtain their individual client authentication tokens.

> [!IMPORTANT]

Microsoft recommends using declarative device management (DDM) to manage and install Apple software updates. For more information about this transition, see the [Intune Customer Success blog: Move to declarative device management for Apple software updates](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/intunecustomersuccess/support-tip-move-to-declarative-device-management-for-apple-software-updates/4432177).

You can use Microsoft Intune to manage software updates for macOS devices that enrolled as [supervised devices](../../device-enrollment/apple/methods-macos.md#user-approved-enrollment). With these MDM-based policies, you can:

- Remotely manage how downloads, installations, and notifications should occur when the following types of updates are available:

  - Critical update
  - Firmware update
  - Configuration file update
  - All other updates (OS, built-in apps)
- Create a schedule that determines when the update installs. Schedules can be simple, like installing updates the next time that the device checks in. Or, you can create day-time ranges when updates can install or when they're blocked from installing.

By default, devices check in with [Intune about every 8 hours](../../device-configuration/troubleshoot-device-profiles.md#policy-refresh-intervals). If an update is available through an update policy, the device downloads the update. The device then installs the update upon next check-in within your schedule configuration.

This feature applies to:

- macOS 12 - macOS 15 (supervised)

On Android Enterprise devices, you can use the **General > Block location** in the [settings catalog](../device-configuration/settings-catalog/ref-android-settings.md) to disable the location services on the device and prevent users from turning it on.
This setting is now called **Location** and has three options you can configure:
- Device default - Intune doesn't change or update this setting. By default, the OS allows end users to turn location services on or off.
- Location enabled - Requires location services to be on and prevents end users from turning them off.
- Location disabled - Requires location services to be off and prevents end users from turning them on.
For a list of all the settings you can configure, see [Android Intune settings catalog settings list](../device-configuration/settings-catalog/ref-android-settings.md).

updates.title: Pre-provision Microsoft Entra hybrid join: Increase the computer account limit in the Organizational Unit (OU)
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Increase the computer account limit in the Organizational Unit (OU)”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.
updates.before:
> - The administrator that installed and configured the Intune Connector had appropriate rights as outlined above, but the [Managed Service Account (MSA)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/understand-service-accounts#standalone-managed-service-accounts) could not be granted permission to create computer objects in the organizational unit(s) specified during the Intune Connector installation. For more information, see [Configure the new Microsoft Intune connector for Active Directory with the least privilege principle](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/intunecustomersuccess/configure-the-new-microsoft-intune-connector-for-active-directory-with-the-least/4432478).
With default permissions in Active Directory, domain joins by the Intune Connector for Active Directory might initially work without any permission modifications to the OU in Active Directory. However after MSA attempts to join more than 10 computers to the on-premises domain, it would stop working because by default, Active Directory only allows any single account to join up to 10 computers to the on-premises domain.
If the administrator installing or configuring the Intune Connector for Active Directory doesn't have the necessary permissions to set permissions on the OUs, then the following steps need to be followed:
1. Sign in to a computer that has access to the **Active Directory Users and Computers** console with an account that as the necessary permissions to set permissions on OUs.
3. Expand the desired domain and navigate to the organizational unit (OU) that computers are joining to during Windows Autopilot.
   > The OU that computers join during the Windows Autopilot deployment is specified later during the **Configure and assign domain join profile** step.

[Excerpt shortened — open the full change for the rest.]

updates.title: Deploy Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices by using Intune and Windows Autopilot
updates.summary: The captured documentation changed in “Requirements; Set up Windows automatic MDM enrollment”. Compare the actual removed and added wording below.

- **Device enrollment** - device enrollment requirements.
- **Intune connector** - Intune Connector for Active Directory requirements.

- If using Proxy, Web Proxy Auto-Discovery Protocol (WPAD) Proxy settings option must be enabled and configured.
- Undergo the out-of-box experience (OOBE).

The device you enroll must meet these requirements:
- If using a proxy, enable and configure the Web Proxy Auto-Discovery Protocol (WPAD) proxy settings option.
